category_title: At-risk students with learning disabilities who are shy and struggle to articulate ideas from print text
scenario_title: Grasping abstract historical concepts and emotional depth
minimal_context: The student is reading a poem and reviewing blackboard notes about the Holocaust during an introductory lesson to connect with the subject material.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please read the poem 'First They Came for the Jews' and look at the information I jotted down on the blackboard about the Holocaust. Write down your thoughts on the worksheet.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks down at the paper quietly) I felt confused by the poem at first and then we reread it and I understood it a little better.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: That's a start. Keep looking at the text and the notes on the board. What do you think about why they were targeted?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Shrugs slightly) I'm not sure. I know they were hated and segregated in Germany, but it's hard to picture.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try to think about the reading and connect to the subject material. What else stands out to you?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I just don't get it. Why didn’t any of the people stick up for themselves?

STUDENT: (Shrugs slightly) I'm not sure. I know they were hated and segregated in Germany, but it's hard to picture.

TUTOR: Just try to think about the reading and connect to the subject material. What else stands out to you?

task.content: Introductory lessons – which included reading, discussing and jotting down information about the Holocaust on the blackboard.
task.learning_goal: Have the class personally connect to the subject material.

context.materials: Blackboard, KWL chart, sheet of paper with quotes from Night, film 'Escape from Sobibor'

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: Attempting to comprehend the curriculum and connect on an emotional level through introductory reading and blackboard notes.
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Amy wanted to know: ‘Why didn’t any of the people stick up for themselves?’ She and her peers conveyed that they could not fully grasp just how deep the anti-Semitism was.
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Trouble comprehending the curriculum and connecting on an emotional level.
related_quotes: Why didn’t any of the people stick up for themselves?

behavior_patterns.condition: Reading and responding to the poem 'First They Came for the Jews'.
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Exhibited much confusion about why Jews were targeted, hated and segregated in Germany at the time of the Third Reich.
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Felt confused by the poem at first.
related_quotes: I felt confused by the poem at first and then we reread it and I understood it a little better.
